thread:
Sophia (Support): FYI customer AcmeCorp is seeing p95/p99 regressions after we pushed a quantization profile change yesterday night. They reported endpoint /v1/generate model=rwd-llama-13b-qprof-v2, p95 jumped from ~600ms to ~2.3s and p99 spikes to 6-8s. They attached request ids: rq_A1, rq_A7, rq_B2.
Jamal Patel: thanks — do we know which config was toggled? qprof-v2 means int8 auto-calibration was enabled, right?
Sophia (Support): yes per change log it flipped from "quant_profile: qprof-v1 (fp16)" -> "quant_profile: qprof-v2 (int8-auto)" at 02:12 UTC. Customer said degradation started ~02:30.
Maria Chen: int8 auto-cal can definitely change kernel paths and force different attention kernels; if calibration wasn't representative it can hit cache/memory thrash or kernel fallbacks that are slower. Any slow logs or OOMs?
Sophia (Support): customer logs show no OOMs. They did send a small stacktrace that shows repeated fallback notices: "WARN: kv_cache_fallback_to_fp16 for shard 3" repeated.
Alex Rivera: that fallback spam is suspicious — likely quantization produced out-of-range values for some layers causing runtime to route to slower fp16 paths per our fallback policy. We should confirm the in-service fallback metric and why fallback fires repeatedly instead of failing fast.
infra-bot: [alert] rolling-p95-anomaly detected on service=runtime-serving region=us-west1 metric=p95_latency threshold=1.2s started=2026-03-14T02:35:12Z
Lee Wong: can we repro internally? steps for support to hand to eng: exact model id, endpoint, a sample prompt that triggers the issue, and the exact request headers (content-type/seq-len).
Sophia (Support): provided sample prompt (short chat prompt ~120 tokens) and full curl:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"rwd-llama-13b-qprof-v2","input":"Summarize quarterly revenue...","max_tokens":256}'
```
Jamal Patel: I'll run under a trace with nvtx and also enable detailed kernel timing. Also checking our runtime logs for "kv_cache_fallback" and query the metric `runtime_quant_fallback_count{model="rwd-llama-13b-qprof-v2"}`.
Maria Chen: parallel thought — if calibration dataset didn't include short-context requests, the scales might be off for typical customer prompts causing numerical instability on a subset of ops. Suggest two mitigations: 1) flip customer to fallback_precision: fp16 for now; 2) re-run calibration with a mixed-length sample and produce qprof-v2b.
Alex Rivera: operational mitigations: immediate canary rollback for AcmeCorp route to qprof-v1 (fp16) or set route to `force_precision: fp16` in routing policy to avoid full rollback. That should restore p95 quickly. We can schedule a full rollout for an updated qprof once MQs are clean.
Sophia (Support): AcmeCorp asked for a timeline, they are fairly sensitive. Can we do a hotfix today?
Lee Wong: yes — I'll prepare a canary change for their customer-id-specific route. Jamal, can you confirm the canary change commands?
Jamal Patel: runbook (quick):
1) create routing override: `redwood route update --customer acmecorp --model rwd-llama-13b --override '{"quant_profile":"qprof-v1","force_precision":"fp16"}'`
2) deploy canary to 5% traffic and watch p95/p99 for 15m
3) if stable, increase to 100% and remove override flag
I'll run step 1 now.
deploy-bot: started deploy 2026-03-14T03:10:02Z user=Jamal status=canary target=acmecorp traffic=5%
Jamal Patel: pushing now — also enabling tracing header `x-redwood-debug=1` so we can correlate slow requests.
Sophia (Support): sent customer the canary note and asked them to ping if they still see slowness. :pray:
infra-bot: [metric] runtime_quant_fallback_count{model="rwd-llama-13b-qprof-v2"} spiked to 420 in 30m (baseline ~2).
Maria Chen: that confirms widespread fallback. After canary we should also run synthetic load with short and long contexts to reproduce fallback noise locally. I'll prepare a calibration run:
```
python tools/calibrate_quant.py
  --model rwd-llama-13b --dataset samples/mixed_lengths.jsonl
  --out qprof-v2b --precision int8 --batch 2
```
and then run inference smoke tests comparing latency: `bench/latency_test --model rwd-llama-13b --profile qprof-v2 qprof-v2b qprof-v1`
Alex Rivera: other quick checks: kernel selection logs `kernel_choice.log` and `kv_cache_hit_rate` — if fallback is due to difference in KV cache alignment we will see low kv hit rates and repeated cache misses causing extra memory thrash. Also confirm CUDA kernel time for attention op increased in fallback path.
Jamal Patel: can confirm after canary metrics: p95 for AcmeCorp dropped from 2.3s -> 580ms after override to fp16. p99 also improved to ~1.1s. Will hold at 5% for 20m then ramp.
Sophia (Support): customer reports improvement. They forwarded one of the previous slow request traces; Jamal, any smoking gun?
Jamal Patel: trace shows attention kernel falling back to slower implementation and repeated buffer reallocs: log excerpt: `WARN kernel_fallback attention_impl_f32 -> attention_impl_fallback_fp16 realloc buf_size=...` — looks like quantized kernels produced inconsistent tensor shapes or ranges causing fallback and reallocs.
Maria Chen: that's consistent with poor calibration. We'll retire qprof-v2 from global rollout and prepare qprof-v2b with improved calibration samples and an extra post-calibration validation step that runs a small latency/accuracy test against a representative workload.
Lee Wong: ops action items:
- rollback global rollout flagged (if any).
- apply route override for impacted customers until qprof-v2b validated.
- add an alert on `runtime_quant_fallback_count` > 10/min per model (to catch regressions earlier).
Alex Rivera: engineering action items:
- add post-calibration validation in the qprof generation pipeline (latency/kv-cache-check).
- add defensive guard in runtime: if fallback rate > X and p95 regresses > Y, prefer stable precision for N minutes instead of per-request fallback noise.
Maria Chen: I'll own the calibration rerun and validation. Jamal will own runtime guard. Lee please own routing overrides and alert rules.
Sophia (Support): I'll update the customer with timeline: hotfix applied, ramping to 100% now, full rollback removed when qprof-v2b validated. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary ramp to 100% complete user=Jamal time=2026-03-14T03:32:12Z
Jamal Patel: follow-up: after ramp to 100% with fp16 override, global p95 for that model returned to baseline. I'll keep tracing on for a few hours and post a follow-up once qprof-v2b completes validation.
Sophia (Support): closing loop with AcmeCorp — asked if they'd like advance notice next time we toggle quant profiles for their route. They requested opt-out for auto-cal toggles until the new validation is in place.
Maria Chen: noted. I'll also add a regression test to the qprof CI that runs a small mix of prompts including their sample to ensure we don't regress in the future.
Alex Rivera: nice quick mitigation — big win. Recommend a postmortem note in #incidents once qprof-v2b rollout plan has dates.
Sophia (Support): will do.
